final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor narrowed the certification claim in a way that is more policy-aware, but that narrowing is a reinterpretation of the same record, not genuinely new admissible evidence. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed; rollout is limited to 6% with rollback and monitoring; the field-service dispatch segment remains below target and exposed; the only risk-acceptance artifact is an unsigned draft that does not cover that exposure; and policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance, while preserving disclosure duties. That means the case for launch may be operationally understandable, but the compliance predicate remains unresolved. This is not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat here is not merely a disclosure nuance or bounded limitation in an otherwise satisfied control set; it is an unmet policy condition tied to an exposed named launch use case. The Actor's response appropriately concedes that monitoring and rollback do not cure the gap, which reinforces rather than resolves the original concern.
remaining_concerns: The affected field-service dispatch use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no signed risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of the field-service dispatch segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed for this named launch use case.
Policy text states rollout controls and post-launch monitoring are not substitutes when the affected segment remains exposed without exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance.
